acs.AC-001.1: WHEN a request to the Jira App API carries a FIT whose signature verifies against Atlassian's JWKS, whose issuer is , whose audience equals the configured app id, which is within its / window, and whose  is the cloudId of a Workspace's Jira site, THE tracker SHALL pass the request to its handler with the cloudId, the Workspace and the principal (if any).
acs.AC-001.2: IF the  header is missing or is not a Bearer token, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 401 with MSG08 without calling the handler.
acs.AC-001.3: IF the FIT signature does not verify, or its key id is unknown after one JWKS refresh, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 401 with MSG08.
acs.AC-001.4: IF the FIT issuer is not  or its audience is not the configured app id, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 401 with MSG08.
acs.AC-001.5: IF the FIT is expired or not yet valid, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 401 with MSG08.
acs.AC-001.6: IF the FIT is valid but its cloudId is not the cloudId of any Workspace's Jira site, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 403 with MSG08.
acs.AC-001.7: THE tracker SHALL never write a FIT or a system token to a log or to an error response.
acs.AC-001.8: IF Atlassian's JWKS cannot be fetched and no cached key matches, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 503 with MSG06 and record the error type.
acs.AC-002.1: WHEN the workspace package registers a site address for a Workspace, THE tracker SHALL read the site's cloudId from Atlassian and store the address and cloudId for that Workspace.
acs.AC-002.2: IF the site address is not an  address, THEN THE tracker SHALL reject it with MSG61 without calling Atlassian.
acs.AC-002.3: IF Atlassian does not return a cloudId for the address (unknown site, network error, timeout of 10 seconds), THEN THE tracker SHALL reject it with an error type the workspace package can show, and keep the Workspace's previous site.
acs.AC-002.4: WHEN a Workspace registers a new site address, THE tracker SHALL replace its previous site so that calls from the old cloudId are refused.
acs.AC-002.5: IF the cloudId is already the site of another Workspace, THEN THE tracker SHALL reject it with MSG61.
acs.AC-003.1: WHEN an "issue created" event arrives, THE tracker SHALL record it as RECEIVED with the cloudId, issue id, issue key, event type, the encrypted system token and the receive time, and respond 202.
acs.AC-003.2: WHEN an "issue updated" event arrives whose changelog contains a  change, THE tracker SHALL record it as RECEIVED in the same way and respond 202.
acs.AC-003.3: WHEN an "issue updated" event arrives whose changelog contains no  change, THE tracker SHALL respond 202 without recording it.
acs.AC-003.4: IF an event that is already recorded is delivered again, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 202 without recording it a second time.
acs.AC-003.5: IF an event arrives without the  header, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 400 with MSG06 and not record it.
acs.AC-003.6: IF the event body is not a valid issue event (no issue id or key), THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 400 with MSG06 and not record it.
acs.AC-003.7: WHEN the tracker records an event, THE tracker SHALL record it under the Workspace whose registered site has the event's cloudId.
acs.AC-004.1: WHILE an event is RECEIVED and due, THE tracker SHALL claim it so that only one worker processes it at a time.
acs.AC-004.2: WHEN the tracker processes an event, THE tracker SHALL read the issue from Jira with that event's system token: key, summary, description, issue type, priority, project key, status with its status category, resolution, created and resolution dates, reporter accountId, and assignee accountId and display name.
acs.AC-004.3: IF the issue's project key does not belong to a T-Solve Project of the site's Workspace, THEN THE tracker SHALL mark the event IGNORED and do nothing else.
acs.AC-004.4: IF an "issue updated" event's issue is not in the Done status category when read, THEN THE tracker SHALL mark the event IGNORED.
acs.AC-004.5: IF processing fails with a retryable error (Jira 5xx or 429, timeout, a dependency unavailable), THEN THE tracker SHALL schedule the event again after 1, 5 and 15 minutes, and mark it FAILED with the error type after the third retry fails.
acs.AC-004.6: IF processing fails with a non-retryable error (Jira 401, 403 or 404), THEN THE tracker SHALL mark the event FAILED with the error type at once.
acs.AC-004.7: IF an event is still unfinished 2 hours after it was received, THEN THE tracker SHALL mark it FAILED with the error type  and delete its token.
acs.AC-004.8: WHEN an event becomes PROCESSED, IGNORED or FAILED, THE tracker SHALL delete its stored system token.
acs.AC-004.9: WHILE the tracker processes an event, THE tracker SHALL read and change only data of that event's Workspace.
acs.AC-005.1: WHEN a created ticket of a T-Solve Project is processed, THE tracker SHALL pass it to triage, ask search to compute and store suggestions for it, and record the triage decision for the panel.
acs.AC-005.2: WHEN triage classifies the ticket as Simple with a suggested solution, THE tracker SHALL add one comment to the ticket with MSG80 filled with the suggested solution and the related Wiki document links, visible to the reporter and with no link to the tickets whose Solutions the suggestion was built from, then mark the event PROCESSED.
acs.AC-005.3: WHEN triage classifies the ticket as Complex or Sensitive, or gives no suggested solution, THE tracker SHALL add no comment and mark the event PROCESSED.
acs.AC-005.4: IF the event is processed again after the MSG80 comment was added (a retry after a later step failed), THEN THE tracker SHALL not add a second comment.
acs.AC-005.5: IF triage returns no related Wiki document links, THEN THE tracker SHALL post MSG80 without its "Related documents" sentence.
acs.AC-006.1: WHEN an "issue updated" event of a T-Solve Project is processed and the issue is in the Done status category, THE tracker SHALL read all of the issue's comments (every page) and pass the issue, comments and assignee to the ticket package to create or update the AI draft, then mark the event PROCESSED.
acs.AC-006.2: IF the ticket package cannot create the AI draft, THEN THE tracker SHALL mark the event PROCESSED and the panel data SHALL report the draft as unavailable (MSG67).
acs.AC-006.3: THE tracker SHALL add no comment to a ticket that moves into the Done status category.
acs.AC-007.1: WHEN a principal linked to an active T-Solve user requests panel data for an issue of a T-Solve Project, THE tracker SHALL return the stored suggestions (as search allows that user, including MSG76 when search is not available to them), the triage decision if any, and the Solution Form state from the ticket package: AI draft or MSG67, unsubmitted draft (MSG77), submitted and awaiting review (MSG65), or changes requested (MSG64).
acs.AC-007.2: IF the principal is not linked to a T-Solve user, THEN THE tracker SHALL return panel data that only asks the user to sign in (MSG62), plus the MSG81 question when STORY-010 applies.
acs.AC-007.3: IF the principal is linked to a deactivated T-Solve user, THEN THE tracker SHALL return panel data with MSG10 and nothing else.
acs.AC-007.4: IF the issue's project is not a T-Solve Project, THEN THE tracker SHALL return panel data that says the project is not connected, with no suggestions.
acs.AC-007.5: WHEN a linked active user asks to search again, THE tracker SHALL read the issue's current summary and description from Jira, ask search to recompute suggestions, and return them.
acs.AC-007.6: IF search or Jira does not answer within 20 seconds, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 503 with MSG06.
acs.AC-008.1: WHEN a linked active user saves the Solution Form as a draft, THE tracker SHALL pass it to the ticket package with that T-Solve user as author and return the result.
acs.AC-008.2: WHEN a linked active user finishes the Solution Form, THE tracker SHALL pass it to the ticket package with that T-Solve user as author and return the result.
acs.AC-008.3: WHEN a linked active user closes the Solution Form opened after resolving the issue, THE tracker SHALL submit an empty Solution for review through the ticket package (MSG70).
acs.AC-008.4: IF the principal is not linked to an active T-Solve user, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 403 with MSG62 and not call the ticket package.
acs.AC-008.5: IF the ticket package rejects the request, THEN THE tracker SHALL return its error and message code unchanged.
acs.AC-009.1: WHEN the daily clean-up runs, THE tracker SHALL delete PROCESSED, IGNORED and FAILED events received more than 30 days earlier.
acs.AC-009.2: THE tracker SHALL not delete RECEIVED events during clean-up.
acs.AC-009.3: IF the clean-up fails, THEN THE tracker SHALL record the error type and leave the rows for the next daily run.
acs.AC-010.1: WHILE an issue has an MSG80 suggestion with no answer yet and the principal is the issue's reporter, THE tracker SHALL include the MSG81 question in the panel data, even if the principal is not linked to a T-Solve user.
acs.AC-010.2: WHEN the reporter answers Yes or No, THE tracker SHALL pass the answer to triage and return MSG82 for Yes or MSG83 for No.
acs.AC-010.3: IF the principal is not the issue's reporter, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 403 with MSG08 and not record an answer.
acs.AC-010.4: IF the issue has no MSG80 suggestion or it was already answered, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 409 with MSG06 and not record an answer.
